mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate compresses discount rates for equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower borrowing costs and increased corporate investment.
failure_condition: In 20-day forward periods following a 3-month FEDFUNDS decline, S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 55% of cases or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, S&P 500 produces positive 5-day forward returns in more than 55% of instances or Rank IC is negative over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates broad-based demand weakness, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate revenue expectations decline.
candidate_trigger: HOUST MoM decline > 0.5% and RSAFS MoM decline > 0.3%
failure_condition: When HOUST MoM decline > 0.5% and RSAFS MoM decline > 0.3%, S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100), which signals manufacturing contraction, S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors price in reduced corporate output and profit margins.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 100, S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 55% of cases or Rank IC is negative over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI inflation exceeds 3.5%, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.5%, S&P 500 produces positive 5-day forward returns in more than 55% of instances or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In 60-day forward periods following a 3-month PAYEMS increase, S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 55% of cases or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong consumer demand (RSAFS > 750000 million dollars), S&P 500 experiences positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate revenue growth and investor confidence improve.
failure_condition: When RSAFS > 750000, S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns in more than 55% of cases or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%) and stable federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 3.5%) signals active monetary tightening, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS > 3.5%, S&P 500 produces positive 5-day forward returns in more than 55% of cases or Rank IC is negative over any 1-year rolling window.
